41-reaction-library.png: Reaction library: net photosynthesis equation with species cards linked to the 3D molecule viewer, machine-checked atom/charge balance, net-equation caveats and registry connections (Biologic processes shown as planned, not as working links).
42-equation-validation.png: User equation “N₂ + O₂ → NO₂” balanced exactly (rational null space) to N₂ + 2 O₂ → 2 NO₂ but flagged “not verified” because it is not in the curated library; background: permanganate/iron(II) redox with charge (+17 = +17) conserved.
40-source-index.png: Source index (#/sources): every citation behind the app — peer-reviewed articles, academic texts, national laboratories and standards bodies — with DOI/official link, institution, licence, a verified author note and what it is used for. Reached here from a reaction’s source link.
43-thermochemistry-energy-diagram.png: Haber–Bosch thermochemistry at 298.15 K from CODATA Key Values: ΔrH° = −91.88 ± 0.70 kJ/mol, ΔrS°, ΔrG°, K; the energy diagram puts elements, reactants and products on one enthalpy axis (Derived), while the dashed path is Illustrative and has no barrier value. Each species row lists its value, uncertainty and source.
43b-thermochemistry-700K.png: Same reaction at 700 K: ΔrG° becomes positive (K < 1). This is why industrial ammonia synthesis trades yield for rate, and the panel warns that the constant-ΔH/ΔS approximation applies.
44-crystal-lattice-rutile.png: Rutile TiO₂ 2×2×2 supercell from the NBS Circular 539 lattice constants (transcribed and flagged) with O positions from Abrahams & Bernstein (1971). It shows the unit-cell edges, nearest-neighbour bonds and a (110) plane. Computed X-ray density 4.250 g/cm³ matches the NBS value. TiO₆ coordination is derived, and the Bragg table marks systematic absences.
44b-crystal-lattice-nacl.png: Halite (NaCl) 3×3×3 supercell with the (111) plane: 6-fold Na–Cl coordination at a/2 = 2.820 Å, and a computed density within 0.1 % of NBS.
45-material-properties-silica.png: Fused silica: refractive index n(λ) from Malitson’s (1965) Sellmeier formula (n_D = 1.4585, blank outside 0.21–6.7 µm). Properties without a cited source (emissivity, permeability, absorption) show as unknown.
45b-material-properties-copper.png: Copper: fcc cell (NBS), JANAF Cp(T) approaching the Dulong–Petit 3R line, and the 100 % IACS resistivity standard (1.7241 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m at 20 °C) labelled as a defined reference value.
45c-material-properties-water.png: Water at 293 K and 1 atm: speed of sound, density, cp, viscosity and thermal conductivity from the NIST reference equation of state (IAPWS-95), static permittivity from Malmberg & Maryott (1956), and Daimon & Masumura dispersion.
46-phase-diagram-water.png: Water phase diagram: vaporisation from IAPWS SR1-86, melting curves of ice Ih/III/V/VI/VII and sublimation from IAPWS R14-08 (each drawn only within its validity range), triple and critical points. The probe at 373.124 K, 1 atm lists the coexisting liquid and vapour (IAPWS-95 via NIST): density, speed of sound and the latent heat.
46b-phase-diagram-co2.png: CO₂ phase diagram: Span–Wagner coexistence curve, sublimation from the Antoine fit to Giauque & Egan (1937) only inside 154–196 K (the gap to the triple point is shown, not interpolated), and the melting curve marked “not bundled”. A liquid probe is flagged uncertain for that reason.
47-lennard-jones-liquid.png: Qualitative Lennard-Jones fluid (256 atoms, argon parameters from Rahman 1964), thermostatted at 120 K and ρ = 1.35 g/cm³. Shown: live liquid-like g(r), the LJ potential with its 2^{1/6}σ minimum, and observables. Labelled Simulated and qualitative, with playback speed kept separate from simulated time.
47b-lennard-jones-solid.png: Same model in the solid preset (ρ* = 1.1, T = 60 K): fcc lattice vibrations, and a g(r) with sharp crystalline peaks.
48-wave-lab-transverse.png: Wave laboratory: a transverse travelling wave on a string. v = √(T/μ) = 100 m/s comes from the medium, so λ = v/f = 4 m is derived and not independently adjustable. Shown: a snapshot y(x), the probe trace y(t), and playback (slow motion) kept separate from physical time.
48b-wave-lab-longitudinal.png: Longitudinal 440 Hz sound wave in dry air at 20 °C: c = √(γRT/M) = 343 m/s, with M derived from the NSSDC composition. Particles oscillate along the direction of travel, and colour marks compression and rarefaction. λ = 0.780 m.
48c-wave-lab-interference.png: Superposition of two co-propagating 25 Hz waves with a phase difference of π (destructive interference): amplitudes 5 mm and 3 mm leave a 2 mm resultant.
48d-wave-lab-standing.png: Standing wave: third harmonic of a 1.2 m string fixed at both ends. f₃ = 3v/2L = 125 Hz, with nodes at both ends and two interior nodes.
48e-wave-lab-two-source.png: Two coherent 50 kHz ultrasound sources in water (c from IAPWS-95 via NIST) 3λ apart: the time-averaged intensity shows bright fringes where the path difference is mλ and dark fringes at (m + ½)λ.
49-spectral-atlas.png: Spectral atlas (#/spectral): the Hg I 253.7 nm line (NIST ASD) placed on a log wavelength/frequency/energy axis. Each band row is a named convention: ITU-R V.431-9 radio bands, CIE S 017 UV/IR, ISO 21348 (overlapping sub-categories stacked) and the detector IR scheme. ISO 20473 is listed as not available because its text could not be consulted. The right panel shows f, E = hf, the wavenumber, the band name under each convention, and n(λ) in a chosen material.
49b-plane-wave.png: Vacuum plane wave at 550 nm with right-handed circular polarisation (CIE: clockwise as seen by the receiver). E (red) and c·B (blue) are perpendicular to each other and to k (gold) at every point, with |B| = |E|/c. B₀ and the time-averaged intensity ½cε₀E₀² follow from the chosen E₀.
49c-blackbody.png: Planck spectrum of a 5772 K blackbody (IAU nominal solar T_eff): peak per wavelength 502.0 nm. The per-frequency peak corresponds to a different wavelength (c/ν_max ≈ 883 nm). σ and b are derived from h, c and k and match CODATA. Labelled as a model, not the observed solar spectrum.
49d-atomic-lines.png: Hydrogen (H I) lines from the NIST Atomic Spectra Database on the spectrum, opened from the element view. Selecting Hα (656.46 nm, vacuum) gives its frequency and photon energy and names its band under each convention.
